evidence.reading: One version value is hand-written in at least nine places across four workflows and two Dockerfiles, and three of them are independent OWNERS rather than consumers of a single source. slurm-base-image.yml builds tests/slurm/Dockerfile.base through docker/build-push-action@v7 (:35-44) and passes no build-args, so the version actually compiled is decided solely by the ARG default at Dockerfile.base:42, while the tag pushed at :41 is interpolated from that workflow's own env at :14. Nothing forces the two to agree, so bumping one and not the other publishes an image tagged 4.2.3 that contains a different MPICH. A third owner consumes the result: mpi-slurm.yml:106 pulls slurm-mpich-base:${MPICH_VERSION} resolved from its own env at :33, and tests/slurm/Dockerfile:15 pins the same tag again as a literal in its BASE_IMAGE default. The comment at Dockerfile.base:8 states the rebuild trigger is a change to that file or to MPICH_VERSION in the ci env, but slurm-base-image.yml's path filter (:5-8) watches only tests/slurm/Dockerfile.base and the workflow file itself, so a ci.yml version bump triggers no rebuild and no re-tag. The ch4:ofi device at Dockerfile.base:54 differs deliberately from the ch3:nemesis device the workflow copies configure, so this is a genuinely separate artifact and not a fourth copy of the candidate above.

candidates.fixShape: Give the version one owner and make every other site derive from it. The base-image workflow passes the version to docker/build-push-action as a build-arg so the ARG default in Dockerfile.base stops being an independent decision, and the pushed tag and the built version then come from the same expression. The pinned literal in tests/slurm/Dockerfile's BASE_IMAGE default and the pull in mpi-slurm.yml both take the tag from that same value rather than repeating it. The prose rebuild-trigger claim at Dockerfile.base:8 is then either made true by adding the workflow path that carries the version to the base-image workflow's path filter, or corrected to describe the filter that exists. The composite action proposed for the MPICH step triple takes the version as an input for the same reason, so both fixes converge on one source rather than introducing a second mechanism.

56:## declaration reserved for workspace consistency).

--
crates/cobre-sddp (13 files under src/ and tests/, the only crate with cfg consumers)
--
cobre-core, cobre-solver, cobre-comm, cobre-stochastic, cobre-io, cobre-sddp, cobre-cli, cobre-python
evidence.reading: The declaration at :57 is empty and the comment at :55-56 states both that the crate has no slow tests and that the declaration exists for workspace consistency. Neither half buys anything at the pin. No cfg(feature = "slow-tests") consumer exists outside cobre-sddp: grep over every crate's src and tests matches cobre-sddp alone, so enabling the feature on cobre-cli changes no compilation. The consistency claim is falsified by the workspace itself: only four of the thirteen members declare slow-tests (cli :57, io :19, stochastic :18, sddp :46) while cobre-core, cobre-solver and cobre-comm each have a [features] table and do not declare it, so the property the comment names is not a property the workspace has. The declaration is not load-bearing for any invocation in the tree either. CLAUDE.md:12 and ci.yml:32 pass slow-tests with --workspace, where cargo requires only that some selected member declare the name, and cobre-sddp does; every per-package invocation in the tree that passes the feature targets cobre-sddp (invariance-shuffle.yml:34 and :55, CONTRIBUTING.md:182 and :185 and :583 and :585), so no -p cobre-cli --features slow-tests call exists to break. The remaining effect is that ci.yml's hand-maintained per-crate feature census at :25 advertises slow-tests as a cobre-cli capability, which is how a no-op declaration turns into a claim readers act on.

candidates.fixShape: Delete the empty declaration and its comment from the manifest. Nothing in the tree needs it: the workspace-wide command in CLAUDE.md:12 and the NON_SOLVER_FEATURES string at ci.yml:32 keep resolving through cobre-sddp because cargo asks only that one selected member declare the feature under --workspace, and every per-package invocation that passes slow-tests names cobre-sddp. The hand-maintained feature census comment at ci.yml:25 loses its slow-tests attribution in the same change so the two stay consistent. If the owner instead wants the declaration kept as a deliberate seam, the proportionate change is the opposite direction and belongs to the owner, not to this station: replace the falsified consistency sentence with the actual reason and then declare the feature in the three members that have a feature table and lack it, so the stated invariant becomes true.

evidence.reading: Diffing the member list at Cargo.toml:4-17 against the crate names the publish step actually submits shows exactly five members present in the manifest and absent from the workflow, and they are the five reserved ones. The workflow's ordered list at :80 :84 :85 :86 :90 :94 :98 :103 is written by hand in dependency layers with prose comments, the step that runs it is named Publish all crates at :36, and it ends by echoing All crates published successfully at :105, so both the step name and the success message assert a set five members wider than the list. One omission is documented: an inline comment states that cobre-python goes to PyPI via maturin rather than crates.io, which matches its workspace exclusion at Cargo.toml:21-23. The five reserved members have no such note anywhere in the workflow, and grep finds no publish key in any of their manifests, so nothing in the manifests marks them unpublishable either. Their manifests point the other way: cobre-mcp/Cargo.toml:3 carries the description Reserved crate name. The Cobre MCP server is not yet implemented; depend on cobre-cli for command-line interaction with Cobre, which is prose written for a crates.io reader, and each reserved manifest inherits the workspace version. So the two artifacts disagree about intent and no guard forces the question: if the reserved names are meant to hold their place on the registry, the release never refreshes them; if they are not meant to be published, the manifests do not say so and only a hand-written list keeps them out. Either way, the day a reserved crate becomes real, the publish list stays silent and the release still reports success.

candidates.fixShape: Make the intent explicit at one site and let the workflow derive from it rather than restate it. Either add publish = false to the five reserved manifests, which puts the decision next to the crate it describes and lets the workflow assert that every member is either in its ordered list or marked unpublishable, or add the five to the list at the layer that has no intra-workspace dependencies, which is where they belong since their dependency tables are empty. In both cases the reconciliation is a few lines inside the existing Publish all crates step comparing the member list against the list plus the opt-outs, so the workflow fails loudly instead of echoing success over a silent omission, and no new gate script or framework is introduced. The step name and the closing message are corrected to name the set that is actually published if any member stays out by design.

positives.subject: scripts/ci/lib/comment_scan.sh owns one shared fact and guards it against drift
positives.why: Correct and worth protecting, and it is the model the scan-directory candidate asks to extend. The library holds the cfg(test) boundary regex as a single source of truth (:5-9, the awk at :21-26), documents the two gates that structurally cannot use the streaming helpers and why (:11-14), and carries a guard that runs only when the file is executed rather than sourced (:36-65) so the holdout gates pay no runtime cost while still being checked. That guard is wired blocking at ci.yml:268 as the cfg(test) boundary drift guard step. A duplicated fact with an executable guard and a written reason for every exception is the right shape; the gap is that the crate-directory list next to it has neither.
positives.sanctionedBy: gate-census.json row for scripts/ci/lib/comment_scan.sh (class blocking, wiring .github/workflows/ci.yml:268)

positives.subject: cobre-sddp's slow-tests declaration is the justified instance
positives.why: Examined and clean. crates/cobre-sddp/Cargo.toml:40-46 declares the feature with a rationale naming the specific long-running suites it gates, and it is the only crate with cfg consumers, matching CLAUDE.md:47's three named test families and every per-package invocation in the tree that passes the feature. It is the counter-example that makes the three no-op declarations legible as cost rather than convention, and it should not be swept up with them.

positives.subject: The cobre-python workspace exclusion states its own reason
positives.why: Examined and clean. Cargo.toml:18-20 explains the exclusion before the exclude table at :21-23, and publish.yml repeats the consequence where it matters by noting that the bindings go to PyPI via maturin rather than crates.io. This is the shape the publish-list candidate asks for on the reserved members: an omission that says why it is an omission.

positives.subject: EXCLUDED_FILES=() in the genericity gate is an emptied exemption, not an unused hook
positives.why: Examined and clean. scripts/ci/check-infra-genericity.sh:70-73 records that the value-function-artifact format break retired the former output/policy exemption and that an entry may be added only with owner sign-off, so the empty array at :74 is the retirement rather than a vestige. Same shape as the entry-free allowlist: emptiness with a written reason and a sign-off gate.

positives.subject: The three advisory-by-design gates' terminal exit 0 is declared, not broken
positives.why: Examined and clean. Each advisory gate's ci.yml step carries an ADVISORY comment immediately above it and the script ends in exit 0 on purpose: check-comment-line-refs.sh (comment ci.yml:278-279, exit at :157), check-comment-banners.sh (ci.yml:282-283, exit at :174) and quality-report.sh (ci.yml:298-299, exit at :134). Advisory output with a written declaration is a design choice, so none of them is a finding, and check-comment-bloat.sh inherits that class transitively through quality-report.sh:132.

_needsHuman: Are the five reserved crate names meant to be re-published at every release so they keep holding their place on crates.io, given that their manifests carry crates.io-facing Reserved crate name descriptions and none sets publish = false, or is their absence from the publish list the intended policy that the manifests should be made to state?

Should the three empty slow-tests declarations be kept as a deliberate seam despite no mirror entry and a falsified consistency rationale, in which case the feature also belongs in the three members that have a feature table and lack it, or deleted as the candidates propose?
Is a first composite action under .github/actions/ acceptable, given the directory does not exist at the pin and the change would reshape the release-critical MPI workflows as well as ci.yml?

Routing, not a finding for this lens: scripts/ci/lib/comment_scan.sh:11-14 says two gates cannot use the streaming helpers and names check-comment-banners.sh and check-allow-rationale.sh, while its own drift-guard array at :46-50 carries three holdouts including quality-report.sh; the enumeration mismatch belongs to the drift lens if it is wanted.

P1 MPICH triple: The MPICH Cache/Build/Set step triple is copied byte-for-byte eight times inside ci.yml, with two near-variants in mpi-slurm.yml and release-mpi.yml and no composite action anywhere under .github/

The MPICH version literal 4.2.3 has three independent owners in the SLURM image path (workflow env, Dockerfile ARG default, pushed image tag) and no build-arg links them, so the tag can name a version the image was not built from
P2 slow-tests: cobre-cli declares an empty slow-tests feature with no cfg consumer anywhere in the crate, justified by a workspace-consistency claim that three other members with feature tables falsify
cobre-io declares an empty slow-tests feature with no cfg consumer anywhere in the crate, justified by the same workspace-consistency claim the workspace falsifies
P3 reserved stubs: (positive) The five reserved stub members impose no measurable workspace cost worth raising, so no cost candidate is filed against them
(positive) cargo-dist cannot ship a reserved stub binary because the dist member selection names one package
P4 allowlist: (positive) EXCLUDED_FILES=() in the genericity gate is an emptied exemption, not an unused hook
P5 gate-corpus shape: Five comment and doc gates each hand-maintain their own copy of the crate-source scan-directory list, in two divergent shapes, and four of them do so while already sourcing the shared scan library that exists to hold exactly this kind of shared fact
